_comment: Hand-authored natural-language behavioural queries for Chess-Engine-in-cpp-master. Queries describe behaviour, not identifiers. Labels were assigned by reading the function source in base.json BEFORE any retrieval was run; no retrieval output, embedding, or LLM enrichment was consulted. grade 2 = the function that directly implements the described behaviour; grade 1 = a helper / closely supporting function. Single annotator (AI-assisted authoring); NOT independently reviewed by a second human.

queries.query: Check whether the king of the side to move is currently under attack
Load a position from a Forsyth-Edwards Notation string into the internal board representation
Compute a unique hash key that identifies a chess position
Allocate the transposition table with a size given in megabytes
Look up a previously stored search result for the current position in the hash table
Store a search score together with its bound type and depth in the hash table
Erase every entry in the transposition table
Report how full the transposition table currently is
Detect whether the current position has already occurred earlier in the game
Estimate whether a capture wins or loses material by simulating the sequence of exchanges on a square
Assign scores to candidate moves so the most promising ones are tried first
Pick the highest scored move remaining in a move list
Extend the search past the nominal depth by examining only captures and promotions until the position is quiet
Recursive alpha-beta search that returns the best score for a position at a given depth
Re-run the search with a narrow score window around the previous iteration's result
Search progressively deeper one level at a time until the depth limit or the clock runs out
Work out how much time to allocate to the current move from the remaining clock and increment
Stop the search when the allotted time has been exceeded
Send the GUI the depth, score, node count and principal variation after an iteration
Handle the UCI command that starts a search with time controls or a fixed depth
Handle the UCI command that sets up the board from a start position or FEN followed by a list of moves
Answer the UCI handshake by announcing the engine name and author
Play a move on the board, updating piece positions, castling rights and the hash key
Take back a move that was previously played, restoring the pieces
Generate every pseudo-legal move for the side to move into a list
Compute the static evaluation of a position from material and piece-square tables with a game phase
Count how many bits are set in a 64-bit integer
Return the index of the least significant set bit and clear it
Get the squares attacked by a sliding piece given the blockers currently on the board
Convert a move into long algebraic text such as e2e4
Turn a move string received from the GUI into an internal move object
Print a 64-bit bitboard as an eight by eight grid for debugging
Count the leaf nodes reachable at a given depth to verify that move generation is correct
Precompute attack tables for knights and kings and pawns at engine startup
Fill the tables of pseudo-random numbers used for position hashing
Tell whether the side to move still owns any piece other than pawns and the king
Remember quiet moves that caused a cutoff so they are tried early at the same ply and reward them in a history table
Reset all engine state when a new game starts
Test whether a move captures a piece or promotes a pawn
Extract the origin and destination squares from the packed 16-bit move encoding
Stopwatch that returns elapsed milliseconds since it was started
Reflect a square index across the horizontal midline of the board
Flip a bitboard vertically and swap piece colours to test that the evaluation is symmetric
Follow the principal variation from the previous iteration when ordering moves
Split a string into tokens separated by a given delimiter character
